They argued for the proponents of this view with what is established in the principles of jurisprudence (*al-usul*) regarding carrying the unrestricted (*al-mutlaq*) upon the restricted (*al-muqayyad*).

We have explained the question of carrying the unrestricted upon the restricted in our book *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book), in the sura *an-Nisa'*, in our discussion of His saying concerning the expiation for accidental homicide: ﴿And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then the freeing of a believing neck﴾ [an-Nisa': 92], with our statement there. The summary of the discussion on the conflict between the unrestricted and the restricted is that it has four states:

The first: that their ruling and their cause are both identical, like the blood. Allah restricted it in *al-An'am* by its being poured forth (*masfuh*), in His saying: ﴿unless it be carrion or poured-forth blood﴾ [al-An'am: 145], and left it unrestricted from the condition of being poured forth in *an-Nahl*, *al-Baqarah* and *al-Ma'idah*. In *an-Nahl* He said: ﴿He has only forbidden you carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 115 as cited], in *al-Baqarah* He said: ﴿He has only forbidden you carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 173], and in *al-Ma'idah* He said: ﴿Prohibited to you are carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3, as cited]. The majority of scholars say the unrestricted is carried upon the restricted in this state, where the cause and ruling are identical together. For this reason they did not see the redness that rises on the surface of the cooking pot from the cutting of meat as objectionable, because it is blood that is not poured forth. They said: carrying it upon the restricted is one of the styles of the Arabic language, because they affirm and then omit, relying on what was affirmed. From this is the saying of Qays ibn al-Khutaym al-Ansari:

*"We are content with what we have, and you are content with what you have, and opinion differs."*

Here he omitted *radun* (content, plural) because *radin* (content, singular) points to it. And the saying of Dabi' ibn al-Harith al-Barjami:

*"Whoever's dwelling is in Medina tonight, then I and Qayyar are strangers there."*

The original is: "then I am a stranger, and Qayyar also is a stranger," so he omitted one of the two words because the other points to it. And the saying of 'Amr ibn Ahmar al-Bahili:

*"He cast at me a matter from which I and my father were innocent, and out of hunger he cast it at me."*

(p-214) meaning: I was innocent of it, and my father was also innocent of it. And the saying of an-Nabighah al-Ja'di:

*"The Banu Sa'd have claimed that I am an old man of advanced years, and they did not lie."*

meaning: the Banu Sa'd claimed that I was aged and faded, and they did not lie... and so on.

Some scholars of the principles said that carrying the unrestricted upon the restricted is by analogy (*qiyas*), not by the indication of the wording, which is its most evident basis. It was also said: it is by reason ('aql), which is its weakest and most remote basis.

The second case: the ruling is the same but the cause differs, as in the matter we are discussing. The ruling in the restricted (*muqayyad*) verse and in the unrestricted (*muṭlaq*) verse is one, namely freeing a slave as an expiation (*kaffārah*). However, the cause in each differs: the cause of the restricted verse is accidental killing, and the cause of the unrestricted verse is *ẓihār* (a pre-Islamic form of divorce by likening one's wife to one's mother). Such an unrestricted ruling is qualified by the restricted one according to the Shāfiʿiyyah, the Ḥanābilah, and many of the Mālikiyyah. Accordingly, they stipulated faith (*īmān*) in the expiation for *ẓihār*, qualifying this unrestricted ruling by the restricted one. This is contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah and those who agree with him. They said: The qualification of this unrestricted ruling by the restricted one is reinforced by the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying in the story of Muʿāwiyah ibn al-Ḥakam al-Sulamī (may Allah be pleased with him): "Free her, for she is a believer," and he did not ask him about her, whether she was for an expiation or not. Leaving out questioning in a situation of possibility is treated as equivalent to generality in statements. He said in *Marāqī al-Suʿūd*:

"Treat the omission of questioning
As equivalent to generality in statements."

The third case: the reverse of this, namely the cause being the same while the ruling differs. It was said: the unrestricted is qualified by the restricted in this case. It was also said: no, and this is the view of most scholars. They gave as an example the fast of *ẓihār* and the feeding of the needy for it. Their cause is one, which is *ẓihār*, but their rulings differ, because one of them is an expiation by fasting and the other an expiation by feeding. One of them is restricted by consecutiveness (*tatābuʿ*), which is the fast, and the other is unrestricted from the condition of consecutiveness, which is the feeding. Therefore this unrestricted ruling is not qualified by this restricted one. Those who hold that the unrestricted is qualified by the restricted in this case gave as an example the feeding for *ẓihār*, for it was not restricted by being before they touch (*tamāssā*), although freeing a slave and fasting for it were restricted by His saying: ﴿before they touch one another﴾. So this unrestricted ruling is qualified by the restricted one, and it becomes obligatory that the feeding be before intercourse. Al-Lakhmī gave as an example the feeding in the expiation for oaths, where it was restricted by His saying: ﴿of the average of what you feed your families﴾ [al-Māʾidah: 89], while the clothing was left unrestricted from that qualification in His saying: ﴿or clothing them﴾ [al-Māʾidah: 89]. So this unrestricted ruling is qualified by the restricted one, and it is stipulated that the clothing (p-215) be of the average of what you clothe your families with.

The fourth case: that the two differ in both the ruling and the cause together. There is no qualification in this case by consensus (*ijmāʿ*), and this is clear. This applies when the restricted ruling is single. As for when two restricted rulings are reported with two different restrictions, the unrestricted ruling cannot be qualified by both of them, because their restrictions contradict each other. Rather, they are examined. If one of them is closer to the unrestricted than the other, the unrestricted is qualified by the closer one according to a group of scholars, and so it is restricted by its restriction. If neither of them is closer to it, then it is not restricted by either one, and it remains unrestricted, since there is no preference without a preponderating factor. An example of one being closer to the unrestricted than the other is the fast for the expiation of oaths. It is unrestricted from the condition of consecutiveness or separation, while the fast for *ẓihār* is restricted by consecutiveness in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever does not find [the means], then fasting for two consecutive months﴾ [al-Mujādilah: 4]. The fast of *tamattuʿ* (the combined pilgrimage) is restricted by separation in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever does not find [an offering], then fasting for three days during Ḥajj and seven when you return﴾ [al-Baqarah: 196]. The oath is closer to *ẓihār* than *tamattuʿ* is, because both the fast of *ẓihār* and the fast of oaths are fasts of expiation, unlike the fast of *tamattuʿ*. So the fast of the expiation of oaths is restricted by consecutiveness according to those who hold that view, and it is not restricted by the separation that appears in the fast of *tamattuʿ*.

As for the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: [So fasting three days, consecutively], it is not established, because the Companions reached consensus on not writing "consecutively" (*mutatābiʿāt*) in the ʿUthmānic codices. An example of two restrictions where neither is closer to the unrestricted than the other is the fast of making up Ramadan. Allah, exalted is He, said of it: ﴿then an equal number of other days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], and He did not restrict it by consecutiveness or separation. Yet He restricted the fast of *ẓihār* by consecutiveness and the fast of *tamattuʿ* by separation, and neither of them is closer to the fast of making up Ramadan than the other. Therefore it is not restricted by either one of them, but remains a matter of choice: if one wishes, one may do it consecutively, and if one wishes, one may separate it. And Allah knows best. End of quotation from *Dafʿ Īhām al-Iḍṭirāb ʿan Āyāt al-Kitāb*, with a slight addition for clarity.

(p-232) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And his wives are their mothers﴾.

Ibn Kathir said: That is, in prohibition, respect, reverence, honour and veneration; but it is not permissible to be alone with them, and the prohibition does not extend to their daughters and sisters, by consensus, ending. The point of relevance from it. What has been mentioned, that the meaning of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ being mothers of the believers is their sanctity over them, like the sanctity of a mother, and their respect for them like respect for a mother... etc., is clear and there is no difficulty in it. Supporting this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53]; because a person does not ask his true mother from behind a screen. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Their mothers are none but those who bore them﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 2], and it is known that they (may Allah be pleased with them) did not give birth to all the believers of whom they are mothers. And it is understood from His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And his wives are their mothers﴾, that he ﷺ is a father to them. It has been narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn 'Abbas that they both recited: "And his wives are their mothers, and he is a father to them." This fatherhood is a religious fatherhood, and he ﷺ is more compassionate towards his Ummah than a tender father towards his children. He, may He be exalted and majestic, said of his kindness and mercy towards them: ﴿It grieves him that you suffer; he is anxious over you, and to the believers he is kind and merciful﴾ [at-Tawbah: 128] [33/40]. And it is not a fatherhood of lineage, as He explained by His saying: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾. Also supporting this is the hadith of Abu Hurairah in Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "I am to you only in the position of a father, teaching you. So when one of you goes to relieve himself, let him not face the qiblah nor turn his back to it, and let him not clean himself with his right hand." And he used to command using three stones and forbid bones and dung. So his saying ﷺ in this hadith, "I am to you only in the position of a father," clarifies the meaning of his fatherhood mentioned, as is not hidden.

Issue.

Know that the scholars differed over whether the daughters of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ may be called "sisters of the believers" or not; and whether their brothers, such as Mu'awiyah and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, may be called "maternal uncles of the believers" or not; and whether they may be called "mothers of the believing women"? Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his tafsir of this verse: "The prohibition does not extend to their daughters and sisters, by consensus, although some scholars called their daughters 'sisters of the Muslims,' as is the explicit statement of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, in al-Mukhtasar, and it is from the category of using a general expression, not establishing a ruling. And is it said of Mu'awiyah and his like that he is 'maternal uncle of the believers'? There are two opinions among the scholars, may Allah be pleased with them. al-Shafi'i explicitly stated that it is not said. And are they called 'mothers of the believing women'?"

(p-233) Thus women enter into the masculine sound plural by way of predominance, and there are two opinions on this. It is authentically reported from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "It is not said." This is the more correct of the two views in the school of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him. End of the relevant point from Ibn Kathir's words.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And his wives are their mothers﴾.

This noble verse indicates, by implication (dalalat al-iltizam), that he ﷺ is a father to them, because the motherhood of his wives towards them necessitates his fatherhood ﷺ towards them.

This implied meaning is explicitly stated in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, for he recites: "And his wives are their mothers, and he is a father to them." This reading is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas.

Another verse has come that explicitly contradicts this implied meaning and the irregular reading, which is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Ahzab: 40].

The answer is clear: the fatherhood affirmed is religious, and the fatherhood denied is physical (tiniyyah). By this the difficulty is removed regarding His saying: ﴿And his wives are their mothers﴾ together with His saying: ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53], for it is said: how is a person required to ask his mother from behind a screen?

The answer is what we have just mentioned: they are mothers in prohibition, respect, reverence and honour, but not in being alone with them, nor in the prohibition regarding their daughters and the like. And Allah knows best.

The Qur'anic verse: ﴿And [mention] when We took from the Prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary. And We took from them a solemn covenant.﴾

His statement, may He be glorified and exalted, in this noble verse: He mentions that He took from the Prophets their covenant. Then He singled out five of them for it: they are the Ulul-'Azm (the Messengers of firm resolve) among the Messengers, namely Muhammad (ﷺ), Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. Here He did not specify the covenant He took from them, but He, may He be glorified and exalted, specified it in another place. He specified the covenant taken from all the Prophets in His saying, may He be exalted, in the surah of "Al 'Imran": ﴿And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, and then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said, "Do you affirm and accept My commitment on that condition?" They said, "We affirm it." He said, "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ ﴿And whoever turns away after that — then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 81–82]. We have already presented the discussion of this verse in the surah of "Maryam," in the discussion of the story of al-Khidr. Moreover, He, may He be glorified and exalted, specified the covenant He took from the particular five who are the Ulul-'Azm among the Messengers in the surah of "ash-Shura," in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and that which We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus: "Establish the religion and do not be divided therein."﴾ [ash-Shura: 13].

From what we have mentioned, you know that the verse of "Al 'Imran" and the verse of "ash-Shura" both contain an explanation of this verse of "al-Ahzab."

And His saying in this noble verse: ﴿and from you and from Noah﴾ is an instance of ʿaṭf al-khāṣṣ ʿalā al-ʿāmm (conjunction of the specific upon the general), and we have discussed it repeatedly. And Allah, the Exalted, knows best.

The Words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when hosts came to you, and We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, commands the believers to remember His favor upon them when there came to them hosts, namely the confederate armies (jaysh al-Ahzab). Allah, Majestic and Exalted, sent upon them a wind and armies that the Muslims did not see. These armies that they did not see, by which He bestowed His favor upon them here in Surat "al-Ahzab," He also mentioned that He bestowed them upon them at the Battle of Hunayn, in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And [remember] the day of Hunayn, when your large number pleased you but it did not avail you at all, and the earth was confining for you in spite of its vastness, then you turned back, fleeing.﴾ ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down armies you did not see⦆ [At-Tawbah: 25-26], and these armies are the angels. Allah, Majestic and Exalted, has explained this in "al-Anfal," in the discussion of the Battle of Badr, in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When your Lord inspired to the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast fear into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike [them] above the necks and strike from them every fingertip."﴾ [Al-Anfal: 12]. These armies that they did not see, which are the angels, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, has explained in "Bara'ah" (at-Tawbah) that He supported His Prophet (ﷺ) with them while he was in the cave, in His saying: ﴿If you do not support him, then Allah has already supported him when those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two. When they were in the cave, when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with armies you did not see⦆ [At-Tawbah: 40].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 22:

Allah's saying, the Exalted: ﴿When the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth." And it did not increase them except in faith and submission.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentions that when the believers saw the confederates, meaning the armies of the disbelievers who came upon them from above them and from below them, in the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwat al-Khandaq), they said: ﴿This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth.﴾ Here He does not specify the verse in which He promised them this, but He did clarify it in Surah al-Baqarah, in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while the example of those who passed away before you has not come to you? They were touched by hardship and adversity and were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214]. Among those who said that the verse of al-Baqarah mentioned is clarifying this verse of al-Ahzab (p-235) are Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, and others, and this is evident.

His saying in this noble verse, ﴿And it did not increase them except in faith﴾, is explicit that faith increases, and Allah has stated this in verses of His Book. So there is no basis for disagreement about it given Allah's explicit statement of it, the Exalted, in His Book, in multiple verses; such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That they may increase in faith along with their faith﴾ [al-Fath: 4], and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith﴾ [al-Anfal: 2], and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 25:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved in their rage; they did not obtain any good. And Allah sufficed the believers in the fighting.﴾ In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that He repelled those who disbelieved in their rage, that they did not obtain any good, and that He sufficed the believers in the fighting, namely the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions. Here He does not clarify the means by which He repelled those who disbelieved and by which He sufficed the believers in the fighting. However, He, majestic and exalted, clarified that by His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them a wind and hosts you did not see﴾ [al-Ahzab: 9]. That is, by means of that wind and those hosts He repelled them in their rage and spared you the fighting, as is apparent.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, twofold﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30].

We have already presented the verse that clarifies it at the end of Surah "an-Naml," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be thrown into the Fire. Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾ [an-Naml: 90], and in Surah "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] of life and double [punishment] of death﴾ [al-Isra': 75].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 33, verse 31:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever of you devotes herself (yaqnut) to Allah and His Messenger and does righteous deeds — We will give her her reward twice﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, majestic and exalted, mentions that whoever of the wives of His Prophet ﷺ devotes herself (qanata) to Allah and His Messenger and does a righteous deed, Allah, majestic and exalted, will give her her reward twice. Al-qunut (devotion) means obedience. What Allah, majestic and exalted, promised to whoever of them obeys, namely giving her reward twice in this noble verse, has come in a similar promise for others in other places. Among that is His promise to those of the People of the Book who believed in their prophet and then believed in Muhammad ﷺ, that they will be given their reward twice. This is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the word that they might remember. Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it — they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, "We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it." Those will be given their reward twice﴾ [al-Qasas: 51–54], to the end of the verse.

(p-236) Among that is His promise to all the obedient of His ummah ﷺ that He will give them a double portion (kiflayn) of His mercy, exalted is He. This is in His saying, exalted and majestic is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy and make for you a light by which you will walk and forgive you﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Hadid: 28].

Know that the apparent meaning of this noble verse of surah "al-Hadid", from which one should not deviate, is that the address in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Hadid: 28], is general to all of this ummah, as you see. It is not specific to the believers among the People of the Book, as in the verse of "al-Qasas" mentioned above. That it is general is the verified view, God willing, because of the apparent, immediate meaning of the Qur'an, which no diverting factor has turned away from. As for what al-Nasa'i narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, of restricting this verse of "al-Hadid" to the specific case of the People of the Book, as in the verse of "al-Qasas", it contradicts the apparent meaning of the Qur'an. It is not valid to read it that way except with a proof to which one must return. Although al-Dahhak, 'Utbah ibn Abi Hakim and others agreed with Ibn 'Abbas in this, and al-Tabari chose it.

The correct view in this matter, God willing, is what we have mentioned, because it is known among the people of knowledge that the apparent, immediate meaning of the Qur'an may not be deviated from except by a proof to which one must return.

Ibn Kathir said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When the People of the Book boasted that they would be given their reward twice, Allah, exalted is He, revealed to His Prophet this verse concerning this ummah: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you two portions (kiflayn) of His mercy﴾, i.e., two multiples (did'ayn) ﴿of His mercy﴾, and He added to them: ﴿and make for you a light by which you will walk and forgive you﴾ [al-Hadid: 28]. So He favored them with the light and forgiveness. End quote. Ibn Jarir transmitted it from him, and Ibn Kathir too. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 33, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with a thorough purification.﴾

We have already mentioned, in the introduction to this blessed book, that among the types of clarification (bayan) it contains is that some scholars state an opinion about a verse while the verse itself contains an indication (qarinah) showing that this opinion is not correct. We gave several examples of this in the introduction and in many places throughout this blessed book.

Among the examples we cited in the introduction is our statement there: "Among its examples is the view of some scholars that (p-237) the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) do not enter among his household (ahl al-bayt) in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾. However, the indication of the context is clear that they are included, because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment...﴾ (Al-Ahzab: 28), then He said, in the same address to them: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household﴾, then He said after it: ﴿And remember what is recited in your homes...﴾ (Al-Ahzab: 34), and so on."

The majority of the scholars of usul (the principles of jurisprudence) have agreed that the case that is the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) is definitely included in the ruling, so it is not valid to exclude it by a specifying indicator. It is reported from Malik that its inclusion is only probable (zanniyyat al-dukhul). He alluded to this in Maraqi al-Su'ud (a versified work on usul) with his statement:

"Affirm with certainty the inclusion of those whose case gave rise to the occasion (sabab), and transmit from the Imam a probable view, and you will be right."

Thus the truth is that they are included in the verse. End of quotation from the introduction of this blessed book.

The verification (tahqiq), if Allah wills, is that they are included in the verse, although the verse also covers others from among the household.

As for the evidence that they are included in the verse, it is what we mentioned just now: that the context of the verse clearly shows that it was revealed concerning them.

The verification is that the case that is the occasion of revelation is definitely included, as is established in the usul.

A parallel to the inclusion of wives in the term "people of the household" is His saying, exalted is He, concerning the wife of Ibrahim: ﴿They said: Do you wonder at the command of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the household﴾ (Hud: 73).

As for the evidence that others besides them are included in the verse, it is the hadiths reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said concerning Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them: "They are the people of the household," and Allah's supplication for them was that He remove the impurity from them and purify them thoroughly. A group of the Companions transmitted this from the Prophet (ﷺ), among them the Mother of the Believers Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, Abu Sa'id, Anas, Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', the Mother of the Believers Aishah, and others, may Allah be pleased with them.

From what we have mentioned of the indication of the Qur'an and the Sunnah, you know that the correct view is that the noble verse encompasses the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), and Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them all.

(p-238) Note (tanbih).

If it is said: the pronoun in His saying ﴿to remove from you the impurity﴾ and in His saying ﴿and purify you﴾ is a masculine pronoun, so if the intended were the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) it would have been said: "to remove from you (feminine plural) and purify you (feminine plural)."

The answer comes in two respects. The first: what we mentioned, that the noble verse includes them along with Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and Fatimah, and the people of the Arabic language have agreed on giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine in plurals and the like (taghlib), as is known in its proper place.

The second respect: among the methods of the Arabic language in which the Qur'an was revealed is that a man's wife may be called by the term "household" (ahl), and in view of the word ahl she is addressed with the address of the masculine plural. From this is His saying, exalted is He, concerning Musa: ﴿He said to his household: Wait﴾ (Ta-Ha: 10), and His saying: ﴿I will bring you news﴾ (An-Naml: 7), and His saying: ﴿Perhaps I will bring you a brand from the fire﴾ (Ta-Ha: 10), while the one addressed was his wife, as many have said. A parallel from the speech of the Arabs is the words of the poet:

"If you wish, I will forbid women other than you, and if you wish, I will not taste fresh water nor cold drink."

From what we have mentioned, you know that the statement of whoever says that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are not included in the verse is refuted by the clear context of the Qur'an, and the statement of whoever says that Fatimah, Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn are not included in it is refuted by the hadiths we have indicated.

Some scholars said: the people of the household in the verse are those upon whom charity (sadaqah) is forbidden, and Allah knows best. As for His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household﴾, the verse, it means: He removes the impurity from them and purifies them by what He commands them to obey Him in, and forbids them to disobey Him in, because whoever obeys Allah, He removes the impurity from him and purifies him from sins thoroughly.

Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: "Then he made clear that He only forbade them, commanded them, and admonished them so that the people of the household of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not commit sins, and that they would guard themselves against them through piety. He used the metaphor of 'impurity' (rijs) for sins and 'purity' (tuhr) for piety, because the honour of one who commits abominations becomes soiled and defiled by them, just as his body becomes soiled by filth. As for good deeds, the honour of one who performs them is clean and protected, like a pure garment. In this metaphor (p-239) there is something that repels people of intellect from what Allah dislikes for His servants, and forbids them from it, and encourages them toward what He is pleased with for them, and commands them to do it. 'Ahl al-bayt' is in the accusative either as a vocative or as a form of praise. In this there is clear evidence that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are among the people of his household."
